query: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa, but its high Mo content increases the electronegativity difference and is associated with reduced plasticity. What single intervention could improve its room-temperature compressive strength–plasticity balance without sacrificing its high strength? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the operative mechanism, the predicted change in strength and plasticity relative to the equiatomic disordered-BCC alloy, the conditions and limits under which the effect should occur, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Partially replace Mo with additional Nb (targeting a 10–20 at.% atomic substitution) in the alloy to reduce the local electronegativity difference and lattice distortion while retaining high solid‐solution strengthening.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo disordered BCC high‐entropy alloy in which high Mo content leads to high yield strength (~1719 MPa) but compromised plasticity.
generation.intervention: Reduce the Mo content by substituting 10–20 at.% of Mo with Nb while keeping other elemental ratios equiatomic.
generation.conditions: Process the modified alloy under similar melting/sintering conditions to ensure that the disordered single-phase BCC structure is retained, with room-temperature compressive testing under identical conditions to the original alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: A uniform, disordered BCC matrix with a moderated local chemical environment resulting from a reduced electronegativity gap and less severe lattice distortions.
generation.mechanism: A higher Nb content fosters improved slip behavior and ductility relative to Mo-rich regions by reducing obstacles to dislocation motion. The substitution weakens the brittleness while still benefiting from solid-solution strengthening, thus preserving high yield strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy is expected to maintain a yield strength near ~1700 MPa with a noticeable improvement in ductility—potentially increasing the fracture strain from a very low value to over 15%, without significant phase instability.
generation.baseline: Original equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy with a yield strength of ~1719 MPa and limited ductility due to the high Mo content.
generation.boundary: Substituting more than 20 at.% Mo may reduce the inherent strengthening provided by Mo, and may also risk the formation of secondary phases; therefore, careful compositional and processing control is essential.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimum level of Mo substitution with Nb and its quantitative effect on ductility must be determined through systematic experimental studies.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of alloys with varying Mo substitution levels (0%, 10%, and 20% replacement by Nb) under identical processing conditions, and perform room-temperature compressive testing along with phase analysis (XRD/SEM).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-substituted alloys do not display a statistically significant improvement in ductility (e.g., at least a 50% increase in fracture strain compared to the baseline) while maintaining the yield strength within ±10% of ~1719 MPa, the hypothesis is falsified.

He defined high-entropy alloys (HEAs) as having five or more major elements beneath 5–35 at.%, and minor elements below five at.%. In 2006, he also established four core effects of HEAs []: High-entropy, severe-lattices-distortion, sluggish-diffusion, and the cocktail effect. With the new concepts, scientists are able to develop and expand alloys without restrictions [,,,,]. Some HEAs have been found to have attractive properties on diffusion [], oxidation [], corrosion [], fatigue [], creep [], fracture toughness [], and elevated-temperature strength []. High-entropy superalloys (HESAs) [], eutectic HEAs (EHEAs) [], light-weight HEAs (LWHEAs) [], refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) [], etc. have been proposed and attract increased attention.
